defect_observations.note: thm:p15-student-one-sided-optimal says the caps are cones about the diagonal that 'impose no requirement that every coordinate have the same sign'. The annex proof (annex lines 439-500) does not address this sentence. The upper cap {Z_m > c_+} lies wholly inside the orthant where every coordinate of x - m1 is positive exactly when t_{nu,alpha} >= nu. Examples are n=2 with alpha >= 3/4 and n=3 with alpha >= 1/2 + 1/sqrt(6), about 0.908. That is the regime of Neyman-Pearson 1933 p.319, whose n=3 illustration says 'the cones will be in the quadrant of positive x's'. The remark is true only as a statement about the defining inequality, and the source's quadrant statement and when it holds are not recorded. This is a precision/correctness note and did not decide the C010 verdict.

Per the audit rules, the author scope record spec/research/edition-2026-p15-student-inference.md was not opened. Preservation of 'identified source variants' was checked against the variants the handbook records and against the held sources at the cited pages. These are: 1937 eq.(123) s = e; table probabilities 2(1-alpha) and 1-alpha; 1933 s^2 = V/n with z = T_m/sqrt(nu) and eq.(117); 1935 eqs.(8)-(10), (15)-(18), (19)-(22) and (29)-(31); and the 1937 eqs.(126)-(129) minimization. All agree. Neyman-Pearson 1933's own premise (p.315: moment coefficients satisfying Hamburger's conditions) is not named. The handbook substitutes proved gamma-family completeness, naming only the 1935 orthogonal-polynomial premise.

The definition's class boundaries are worked only indirectly, through the score-fiber counterexample (annex 428-435) and the local comparison over all similar tests (annex 606-608). No passage shows that the one-sided Student test is similar but neither stationary similar nor two-sided unbiased. This is not required by the success condition as read here.
